channel.title: Kirkland Dispatch
channel.description: Kirkland news, once a week, from the Kirkland Dispatch.

item.title: Tonight: a hearing on zoning three city sites as park
item.description: The Planning Commission hears the city's proposal to rezone city-owned land from residential to park at three sites listed in the notice: 10454 Forbes Creek Drive, 10633 132nd Avenue NE and the church property at 13220 NE 132nd Street.

item.title: November 17: a tool library, a legislative agenda and art on utility boxes
item.description: Beyond the second budget hearing we covered last week, the 5:30 PM study session includes an update on the plan for a city tool library.

item.title: What reaches council on December 8
item.description: The calendar puts final adoption of the 2027–2028 budget and the 2027–2032 capital plan on December 8, along with a parking fee amendment, an update to the Lake Washington School District's school impact fees, a Children and Family Services sales and use tax, and a public hearing on the Slate Peak…

item.title: Before the first hard freeze
item.description: An outdoor faucet is the first pipe to freeze.

item.title: Why Kirkland streets get patched so poorly after builders dig them up for utility hookups, and who is responsible for fixing them
item.description: A reader asked why Kirkland streets get patched so poorly after builders dig them up for utility hookups, and who is responsible for fixing them.

item.title: Why Houghton merged with Kirkland instead of staying its own city
item.description: A reader in Houghton also asked why Houghton merged with Kirkland instead of staying its own city.

item.title: What Kirkland is doing about parking near the restaurants for people who cannot walk far
item.description: A reader downtown also asked what Kirkland is doing about parking near the restaurants for people who cannot walk far.

item.title: Council hears the budget on Wednesday, November 4
item.description: The study session opens at 5:30 PM and the regular meeting at 7:30 PM, City Hall, 123 5th Avenue.

item.title: The same night: a station name and minimum wage options
item.description: Council takes up naming the NE 85th Street station area and then minimum wage options as business items.

item.title: A second budget hearing on November 17
item.description: Council takes the second hearing, then the 2027 property tax levy for adoption, on the same evening it reviews a Juanita Pathway feasibility update.

item.title: Small Business Saturday is November 28
item.description: The city will again recognize the day to support local shops.

item.title: Clocks went back, so check the smoke alarms
item.description: Clocks went back Sunday, which is the traditional day to check smoke alarms.

item.title: Who actually makes the big decisions in Kirkland, the city or King County, and how residents can weigh in before a vote
item.description: A reader in Juanita asked who actually makes the big decisions in Kirkland, the city or King County, and how residents can weigh in before a vote.

item.title: The 2027–28 budget is out, and council starts on it today
item.description: The city calls its preliminary budget balanced: current services kept, key infrastructure funded, and two years of operations added for the Kraken Iceplex and Kirkland Community Center.

item.title: November 4: a station name and minimum wage options
item.description: The 7:30 PM meeting opens hearings on the budget, the 2027–2032 capital plan and the preliminary 2027 property tax levy, then takes up naming the NE 85th Street station area and minimum wage options.

item.title: A Catrina procession on Halloween
item.description: The Kirkland Catrina Walk fills Marina Park, 25 Lakeshore Plaza, on Saturday, October 31, 11 AM to 8:30 PM, with the cultural procession at 6 PM. Free; Mundo Catrina presents it for the first time.

item.title: Recycle Right, Saturday, November 14
item.description: 9 AM to 3 PM at Lake Washington Institute of Technology, 11605 132nd Avenue NE: electronics and small appliances, holiday lights, paper for shredding, clothing and linens.

item.title: Quieter mowing at one park
item.description: Parks crews are running electric mowers, edgers and blowers at Phyllis A. Needy Houghton Neighborhood Park in a one-year pilot, reviewed every quarter; it could expand to other parks.

item.title: Property taxes are due Monday this year
item.description: King County's second-half property tax is due October 31.

item.title: What's free to do in Kirkland this month
item.description: A reader in Totem Lake asked what's free to do in Kirkland this month.

item.title: The average utility bill would rise 8.40% in 2027 and 8.35% in 2028
item.description: Final rates were on Tuesday's agenda for adoption: about $284 a month for a typical house in 2027, up $22.03.

item.title: Middle housing: quick fixes first
item.description: State law now allows at least four homes on every residential lot, but they follow single-family size rules.

item.title: Ballot drop boxes are open
item.description: Three boxes in Kirkland take ballots around the clock until 8 PM on Tuesday, November 3: the Wester Lot downtown, Big Finn Hill Park and Kingsgate Library.

item.title: Budget dates
item.description: Council's budget work session is Thursday, October 29, at 3 PM. On Wednesday, November 4, the first public hearings on the 2027–28 budget, the six-year capital plan and the 2027 property tax levy.

item.title: Shared scooters and e-bikes, a second look
item.description: Three councilmembers asked staff to scope a program; every city around Kirkland already has one.

item.title: Alarms and a way out, before the clocks change
item.description: Clocks fall back Sunday, November 1, an easy moment for a household fire check.

item.title: Drop, cover and hold on this morning at 10:15
item.description: Today is the Great ShakeOut, the statewide earthquake drill.

item.title: October 6: the church lease passed; the station name waits
item.description: Council allowed the newly acquired former church in Kingsgate to be leased for a community purpose while the city settles a long-term plan.

item.title: Tuesday, October 20: utility rates, then the budget
item.description: The 5:30 PM study session covers traffic signals, the Green Loop and a middle-housing briefing.

item.title: Northbound I-405 closes in Bellevue this weekend
item.description: All lanes between SE 8th Street and NE 4th Street close from 11 PM Friday, October 16, to 4 AM Monday, October 19, with the SE 8th on-ramp and the Exit 13 off-ramp closed.

item.title: Green Kirkland Week runs October 17 to 25
item.description: Volunteer stewardship events at parks across the city: planting, weeding and mulching to open the planting season.

item.title: Before the first windstorm
item.description: Report a power outage to Puget Sound Energy at 1-888-225-5773, pse.com/outage or the PSE app, not 911; a downed line is the 911 call.

item.title: Tuesday's council: speed limits, a station name, and a downtown housing agreement
item.description: Speed limits were a study session: discussion, no vote.

item.title: October 20: traffic signals, utility rates, and a Kraken lease that moved
item.description: The study session covers traffic signals and the Green Loop; the regular meeting lists utility-rate adoption, the faith-owned lands code and a middle-housing briefing.

item.title: Southbound I-405 closes in Bothell this weekend
item.description: All southbound lanes between SR 527 and SR 522 close from 10 PM Friday, October 9, to 4 AM Monday, October 12, with the NE 195th Street ramps closed.

item.title: A half marathon closes part of Juanita Drive on Saturday, October 17
item.description: About 1,000 runners start and finish at Juanita Beach Park; eastbound NE Juanita Drive closes 7 to 11:30 AM between 93rd and 98th Avenues NE. Cars parked on the course will be towed.

item.title: Halloween on the city calendar
item.description: The Pee Wee Monster Bash, for ages 1 to 5, is Friday, October 30, 10 AM to noon at the North Kirkland Community Center; $18 per child, register at KirklandParks.net or 425-587-3336.

item.title: Before the saw comes out
item.description: Kirkland regulates any tree 6 inches or more in diameter, measured 4.5 feet up the trunk.

item.title: The I-405 / NE 85th Street interchange closes tonight, then again all weekend
item.description: The shutdown called off in September is back on: 9 PM tonight, Thursday, October 1, to 5 AM Friday, then 10 PM Friday, October 2, to 5 AM Monday, October 5.

item.title: Tuesday, October 6: speed limits, a station name, and the Holmes Point overlay
item.description: The 5:30 PM study session takes up citywide speed-limit changes and an emergency management framework.
